title_en: Supreme People's Court Notice on Issuing the Ninth Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en:
1. Institutions of higher education refuse to issue diplomas and degree certificates to students who violate school rules and disciplines. If the students disagree, they may file an administrative lawsuit in accordance with the law.

2. If an institution of higher education makes a decision such as expulsion based on school rules and disciplines that contravene national laws, administrative regulations or rules, the people's court shall not uphold it.

3. When an institution of higher education makes a decision that affects the fundamental rights of a student due to violation of school rules and disciplines, it shall allow the student to present a defense and timely serve the decision after it is made; otherwise, it shall be deemed a violation of legal procedures.
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Publishing the Ninth Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2014] No. 337

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 9 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Case Guidance Work, the Supreme People's Court has compiled cases published in the Gazette of the Supreme People's Court that have guiding significance for the trial and enforcement work of courts nationwide. Upon discussion and decision by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, seven cases (Guiding Cases No. 38-44), including the case of Tian Yong v. Beijing University of Science and Technology concerning refusal to issue a graduation certificate and a degree certificate, are hereby published as the ninth batch of guiding cases for reference in the trial of similar cases.

December 24, 2014

Guiding Case No. 38

Tian Yong v. Beijing University of Science and Technology — dispute over refusal to issue a graduation certificate and a degree certificate

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on December 25, 2014)

Keywords: administrative litigation; issuing certificates; institutions of higher education; scope of acceptance; due process

Ruling Gist

1. Where an institution of higher education refuses to issue a diploma or degree certificate to a recipient of education due to the latter's violation of school rules or discipline, and the recipient disagrees, the recipient may file an administrative lawsuit according to law.

2. Where an institution of higher education makes a decision to expel a recipient of education based on school rules or discipline that contravene national laws, administrative regulations, or rules, the people's court shall not support such a decision.

3. When an institution of higher education makes a decision affecting the fundamental rights of a recipient of education due to the recipient's violation of school rules or discipline, it shall allow the recipient to present a defense and shall serve the decision promptly after its making; failure to do so shall be considered a violation of legal procedures.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 25 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China

Articles 21 and 22 of the Education Law of the People's Republic of China

Article 8 of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The plaintiff, Tian Yong, was admitted to Beijing University of Science and Technology (hereinafter "BUST") in September 1994 and obtained undergraduate student status. On February 29, 1996, during a make-up examination for the course of Electromagnetics, Tian Yong carried a slip of paper with formulas for electromagnetics. During the examination, when he went to the restroom, the slip fell out and was discovered by the invigilator. Although the invigilator did not find that he had actually peeked at the slip, the invigilator immediately stopped Tian Yong's examination in accordance with examination rules. The defendant, BUST, in accordance with the directive of the former State Education Commission on strictly enforcing examination discipline, had issued in 1994 the Urgent Notice on Strict Examination Management (School Issue No. 068 of 1994) (hereinafter "Notice No. 068"). The Notice stipulated that any student caught cheating in an examination would be expelled and have their student status cancelled. Based on this, the defendant determined on March 5, 1996, that Tian Yong's conduct constituted cheating and made a decision to expel him. On April 10 of the same year, the defendant filled out a notice of change in student status, but neither the expulsion decision nor the notice of change in student status was directly declared or served on Tian Yong, nor were procedures for his withdrawal carried out. Tian Yong continued to participate in normal study and school-organized activities as a student of the university. In September 1996, the defendant reissued a student ID card to Tian Yong, and thereafter collected tuition fees from Tian Yong each academic year, registered him, provided him with a living allowance for college students, and arranged for him to participate in graduation internship and design. His thesis advisor collected the graduation design completion fee issued by the school. Tian Yong also took examinations in the name of a student of the university and obtained certificates for passing the College English Test Band 4 and the BASIC language test on computer application proficiency. The defendant did not dispute the fact that during his four years of study at the school, the plaintiff had passed all courses, completed graduation internship, graduation design, and thesis defense, and obtained an excellent graduation thesis and a total graduation score ranking ninth in his class.

In June 1998, when the department of Tian Yong's major submitted the list of students in his class for the award of a bachelor's degree to the defendant, the relevant department of the defendant refused to issue him a graduation certificate on the ground that Tian Yong had been expelled and no longer had student status at BUST, and consequently did not submit Tian Yong's graduation assignment eligibility form to the education administrative department. The department of Tian Yong's major considered that the plaintiff met the conditions for university graduation and for the award of a bachelor's degree, but since at that time the plaintiff was in negotiations with the school over the graduation issue, it temporarily did not sign the degree award list, intending to do so after the student status issue was resolved. The defendant therefore did not include the plaintiff in the list of candidates for a bachelor's degree to be reviewed by the school's degree evaluation committee. Because some teachers from the defendant appealed to the former State Education Commission regarding Tian Yong's case, the Student Affairs Department of the State Education Commission sent a letter to the defendant on May 18, 1998, stating that the defendant's handling of Tian Yong's violation of examination discipline was too severe and recommending a review. On June 10 of the same year, after review, the defendant still maintained its original conclusion. Tian Yong, believing that he met the statutory conditions for a university graduate and that Beijing University of Science and Technology's refusal to issue him a graduation certificate and a degree certificate was illegal, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing.

Judgment

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing rendered an administrative judgment (1998) Hai Xing Chu Zi No. 142 on February 14, 1999: 1. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, Beijing University of Science and Technology shall issue to Tian Yong a four-year undergraduate graduation certificate; 2. Within 60 days from the effective date of this judgment, Beijing University of Science and Technology shall organize the relevant departments, schools, and the degree evaluation committee of the university to review Tian Yong's eligibility for a bachelor's degree; 3. Within 30 days after the effective date of this judgment, Beijing University of Science and Technology shall perform the duty of reporting to the local education administrative department the relevant procedures for Tian Yong's graduation assignment; 4. Tian Yong's other claims are dismissed. Beijing University of Science and Technology appealed, and the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court rendered an administrative judgment (1999) Yi Zhong Xing Zhong Zi No. 73 on April 26, 1999, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The court's effective judgment held that, according to the provisions of Chinese laws and regulations, institutions of higher education have the power to manage student status, to reward or punish recipients of education, and have the duty to issue diplomas and degree certificates on behalf of the state. The relationship between an institution of higher education and a recipient of education is one of educational administrative management. Where a recipient of education disagrees with a management act of the institution that affects the recipient's fundamental rights, the recipient has the right to file an administrative lawsuit, and the institution of higher education is a proper defendant in administrative litigation.

Institutions of higher education lawfully have corresponding educational autonomy, the right to formulate school rules and discipline, and the power to conduct teaching management and impose disciplinary sanctions on students. However, the school rules and discipline they formulate and the teaching management and disciplinary sanctions conducted based thereon must comply with the provisions of laws, regulations, and rules, and must respect and protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties. In this case, the plaintiff's conduct of carrying a slip of paper during the make-up examination constituted a violation of examination discipline. The defendant could have handled it in accordance with the relevant laws, regulations, rules, and the school's relevant provisions. However, the Notice No. 068, upon which the defendant relied to make the expulsion decision, was in conflict with the statutory expulsion conditions provided in Article 29 of the Provisions on the Administration of Students in Regular Institutions of Higher Education. Therefore, the expulsion decision made by the defendant was unlawful.

The expulsion decision concerned the plaintiff's right to education. To fully protect the parties' rights and interests, and based on the principle of due process, the defendant should have served and declared this decision to the party, and allowed the party to present a defense opinion. However, the defendant neither handled it according to this principle nor actually carried out procedures for the plaintiff such as canceling his student status, transferring his household registration, or transferring his files. The fact that the defendant reissued a student ID card and registered the plaintiff in September 1996 should be regarded as the defendant having changed its decision to expel the plaintiff and having restored the plaintiff's student status. The defendant also arranged for the plaintiff to complete four years of study, participate in examinations, internships, and graduation design, and pass the thesis defense. Although these series of acts were specifically performed by some teachers of the defendant and its affiliated departments, as they were all acts within the scope of their duties, the defendant should bear the legal consequences arising from these acts.

The state implements a diploma certificate system. The defendant, as an institution of higher education established with state approval, shall issue corresponding academic certificates to recipients of education who have obtained student status at a regular institution of higher education, received regular education, and completed their studies meeting certain standards and requirements, so as to recognize that the student has the equivalent academic qualifications. The plaintiff met the conditions for a graduate of the above-mentioned higher education institution. The defendant should, in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 1, Item 5 of Article 28 of the Education Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 35 of the Provisions on the Administration of Students in Regular Institutions of Higher Education, issue to the plaintiff a four-year undergraduate graduation certificate.

The state implements a degree system. Degree certificates serve as a measure to evaluate an individual's academic level. The defendant, as an institution authorized by the state to award bachelor's degrees, should, in accordance with legal procedures, award corresponding degrees and issue degree certificates to persons who meet certain academic or professional and technical levels. According to the legal procedures for issuing bachelor's degree certificates set out in Articles 4, 5, and Item 3 of Article 18 of the Interim Measures for the Implementation of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China, the defendant must first organize the relevant departments and schools to review the plaintiff's graduation grades and graduation evaluation materials to determine whether the plaintiff has adequately mastered the basic theories, specialized knowledge, and basic skills of the subject, and whether he possesses the preliminary ability to engage in scientific research work or undertake specialized technical work; only then can it decide whether to nominate the plaintiff to the degree evaluation committee for inclusion in the list of candidates for a bachelor's degree. The degree evaluation committee may, after reviewing the list, pass it, and then the defendant may award the plaintiff a bachelor's degree.

Guiding Case No. 39

He Xiaoqiang v. Huazhong University of Science and Technology — dispute over refusal to award a degree

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on December 25, 2014)

Keywords: administrative litigation; award of academic degrees; institutions of higher education; academic autonomy

Ruling Gist

1. An institution of higher education that has the power to award academic degrees has the right to review an application for the award of a degree submitted by a degree applicant and to decide whether to award the degree. Where an applicant disagrees with a decision of the institution not to award a degree and files an administrative lawsuit, the people's court shall accept the case according to law.

2. Where an institution of higher education, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Interim Measures for the Implementation of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China, formulates academic standards for the award of degrees within the scope of academic autonomy, and makes a decision on whether to award a degree based on such standards, the people's court shall uphold such decision.

Relevant Legal Provisions

1. Article 4 and Paragraph 1 of Article 8 of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China

2. Article 25 of the Interim Measures for the Implementation of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The plaintiff, He Xiaoqiang, was an undergraduate graduate of the class of 2003, majoring in communication engineering, at Wuchang Branch of Huazhong University of Science and Technology (hereinafter "Wuchang Branch"), a third party. Wuchang Branch is an independent public institution legal person and does not have the qualification to award bachelor's degrees. In accordance with the relevant state regulations on awarding bachelor's degrees at privately-run colleges and universities and the agreement between the two parties, the defendant, Huazhong University of Science and Technology (hereinafter "HUST"), agreed to award bachelor's degrees to undergraduate graduates of Wuchang Branch who met the conditions for a bachelor's degree. The appendix to the agreement contained the Detailed Implementation Rules of Huazhong University of Science and Technology for Awarding Bachelor's Degrees to Undergraduate Graduates of Wuchang Branch (hereinafter "Detailed Implementation Rules"). Article 2 of the Detailed Implementation Rules provided: "All undergraduate graduates who have student status at our school and meet the award conditions in these Detailed Implementation Rules may apply to the Degree Evaluation Committee of Huazhong University of Science and Technology for the award of a bachelor's degree." Article 3 provided: "... Those who reach the following levels and requirements, and are reviewed and passed by the academic evaluation committee, may be awarded a bachelor's degree. ... (3) Passing the national College English Test Band 4." In December 2006, HUST issued the Provisions on Applications for Bachelor's Degrees by Wuchang Branch and Wenhua College, which provided that passing the national College English Test (Band 4) was one of the mandatory conditions for non-foreign language majors to apply for a bachelor's degree.

On June 30, 2007, He Xiaoqiang received a Graduation Certificate of a Regular Institution of Higher Education issued by Wuchang Branch. Because he had not passed the national College English Test Band 4 during his undergraduate studies, Wuchang Branch, in accordance with the above-mentioned Detailed Implementation Rules, did not recommend him to HUST to apply for a bachelor's degree. On August 26, He Xiaoqiang applied to HUST and Wuchang Branch for the award of a Bachelor of Engineering degree. On May 21, 2008, Wuchang Branch gave a written reply stating that because He Xiaoqiang had not passed the national College English Test Band 4 and did not meet the award conditions, HUST could not award him a bachelor's degree.

Judgment

The Hongshan District People's Court of Wuhan, Hubei Province, rendered an administrative judgment (2008) Hong Xing Chu Zi No. 81 on December 18, 2008, dismissing the plaintiff He Xiaoqiang's claim requesting the defendant Huazhong University of Science and Technology to issue him a Bachelor of Engineering degree. The Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province rendered an administrative judgment (2009) Wu Xing Zhong Zi No. 61 on May 31, 2009, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The court's effective judgment held that the focus of the dispute in this case mainly concerned whether the administrative act sued was subject to judicial review, whether it was lawful, and the scope of judicial review.

I. The administrative act sued is subject to judicial review. According to the authorization of laws and administrative regulations such as the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China, the defendant HUST has the statutory authority to review and award ordinary bachelor's degrees of regular institutions of higher education. Pursuant to Paragraph 2 of Article 4 of the Interim Measures for the Implementation of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "For institutions of higher education that do not award bachelor's degrees, with respect to undergraduate graduates who meet the academic level for a bachelor's degree, the department shall submit a list to the school, and with the school's consent, the school shall recommend them to the nearest institution of higher education within the same system or region that awards bachelor's degrees. The relevant department of the institution of higher education that awards bachelor's degrees shall review and assess the undergraduate graduates recommended by the institution that does not award bachelor's degrees. If it considers that they meet the requirements of these Interim Measures and relevant regulations, it may nominate them to the school's degree evaluation committee for inclusion in the list of persons to be awarded bachelor's degrees." and in accordance with the relevant policies of the state to promote the running of private colleges and universities, HUST has the right, in accordance with the agreement with the private college, to review and award ordinary bachelor's degrees to undergraduate graduates of private colleges who meet the conditions for awarding bachelor's degrees at this school.

In this case, the third party Wuchang Branch is a private college that has not obtained the qualification to award bachelor's degrees. The college entered into a cooperative school-running agreement with HUST, stipulating that Wuchang Branch would recommend to HUST its undergraduate graduates who met the academic level for a bachelor's degree, and HUST would review and decide whether to award a bachelor's degree. Pursuant to the provisions of the Interim Measures for the Implementation of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China and the cooperative school-running agreement between HUST and Wuchang Branch, HUST has the statutory duty to review the graduating undergraduate students recommended by Wuchang Branch and to decide whether to issue a bachelor's degree. He Xiaoqiang, an undergraduate graduate of Wuchang Branch, filed an administrative lawsuit with the people's court on the ground that HUST had not awarded him a Bachelor of Engineering degree within 60 days from receipt of the application. This complies with the provisions of Paragraph 1 of Article 39 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Interpretation). Therefore, HUST is a proper defendant in this case. Where He Xiaoqiang disagrees with HUST's failure to award him a bachelor's degree and files a lawsuit, the people's court shall accept the case according to law.

II. The provisions of Article 3 of the Detailed Implementation Rules of Huazhong University of Science and Technology for Awarding Bachelor's Degrees to Undergraduate Graduates of Wuchang Branch, formulated by the defendant, are consistent with the higher-level legal provisions. Article 4 of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China provides: "Undergraduate graduates of institutions of higher education who have excellent grades and meet the following academic level shall be awarded a bachelor's degree: (1) having adequately mastered the basic theories, specialized knowledge, and basic skills of the subject ...". Article 25 of the Interim Measures for the Implementation of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China provides: "Degree-conferring units may formulate detailed rules for conferring degrees within their units based on these Interim Measures for Implementation." This Measure grants degree-conferring units the power and duty to formulate standards for awarding bachelor's degrees within the scope of academic autonomy, provided they do not violate the basic principles for awarding bachelor's degrees set out in the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China. Within this authorized scope, HUST's linkage of the national College English Test Band 4 score to the award of a bachelor's degree falls within the realm of academic autonomy. Institutions of higher education, in lawfully exercising their teaching autonomy, may make specific provisions and requirements regarding the quality and academic level of the undergraduate students they cultivate. This is a refinement of the standards for awarding bachelor's degrees and does not violate the principled provisions of Article 4 of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China and Article 25 of the Interim Measures for the Implementation of the Regulations on Academic Degrees of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, because He Xiaoqiang did not pass the national College English Test Band 4 and did not meet the conditions for the award of a bachelor's degree at HUST, Wuchang Branch did not recommend him to HUST for the award of a bachelor's degree. Consequently, there was no omission of duty on the part of HUST, and He Xiaoqiang's claims are not supported.

III. Judicial review of a school's act of awarding a degree is based on the principle of legality review. Different institutions of higher education, based on their own teaching level and actual circumstances, determine their own academic standards for awarding bachelor's degrees within the scope of the basic principles provided by law. This is a concrete manifestation of the principle of academic autonomy in the operation of institutions of higher education. Under the premise that the statutory conditions for awarding degrees are met, whether to set a higher academic standard for awarding bachelor's degrees or to appropriately relax the academic standard is a matter to be decided by each institution of higher education according to its own educational philosophy, actual teaching circumstances, and ideal pursuit of academic level. Judicial review of the award of bachelor's degrees shall not interfere with or affect the principle of academic autonomy of institutions of higher education. The scope of judicial review in administrative litigation concerning the award of degrees shall be based on the principle of legality review.

Guiding Case No. 40

Sun Lixing v. Labor and Personnel Bureau of Tianjin New Technology Industrial Park — dispute over work-related injury recognition

(Discussed and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on December 25, 2014)

Keywords: administrative; work-related injury recognition; work-related reason; workplace; work-related negligence

Ruling Gist

1. The term "work-related reason" as provided in Item 1 of Article 14 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance refers to a connection between the injury sustained by the worker and the worker's own job duties.

2. The term "workplace" as provided in Item 1 of Article 14 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance refers to the place related to the worker's job duties. Where there are multiple workplaces, it also includes the reasonable area where the worker travels between the multiple workplaces during working hours.

3. Where a worker has negligence in performing his own job duties, this does not constitute the circumstances of intentional crime, drunkenness or drug use, or self-injury or suicide as provided in Article 16 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, and does not affect the recognition of work-related injury.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Item 1 of Article 14, and Article 16, of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance

Basic Facts

The plaintiff, Sun Lixing, alleged: He fell and was injured due to work-related reasons during working hours and at the workplace, which falls within the circumstances provided in the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance. The decision of the Labor and Personnel Bureau of Tianjin New Technology Industrial Park (hereinafter "Industrial Park Labor Bureau") not to recognize the injury as work-related was erroneous in fact finding and improper in law application. He requested that the "Decision on Work-Related Injury Recognition" made by the Industrial Park Labor Bureau be revoked, and that the Industrial Park Labor Bureau be ordered to make a new work-related injury recognition.

Defendant, the Park Labor Bureau, argued: Sun Lixing, a business representative of Tianjin Zhongli Lightning Protection Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongli Company), was injured while on a business trip. However, the injury was not caused by work-related reasons but by his own inattention and misstep when descending the stairs. There was no obvious causal relationship between his injury and the work task he had been assigned. Therefore, Sun Lixing did not meet the criteria for recognition as a work-related injury as stipulated in the Regulations on Work-related Injury Insurance. The decision of the Park Labor Bureau not to recognize the injury as work-related was based on clear facts, sufficient evidence, and a lawful procedure, and should be upheld.

The third party, Zhongli Company, stated: Because the company implements a "last-place elimination" system, Sun Lixing had been eliminated before the incident. However, because he had previously been engaged in the company's sales work and still had the obligation to collect outstanding payments, he occasionally returned to the company to make phone calls. At the time of the incident, Sun Lixing was no longer an employee of the company, nor did the fall occur within the company's workplace, and therefore it did not meet the conditions for recognition as a work-related injury.

Facts Found by the Court: Sun Lixing was an employee of Zhongli Company. On the morning of June 10, 2003, he was assigned by the person in charge of Zhongli Company to go to Beijing Airport to pick up a person. He descended from the eighth floor of the International Business Center (hereinafter referred to as the Business Center) in the Huayuan Industrial Park, Nankai District, Tianjin, where Zhongli Company is located, intending to drive the Hongqi car parked in the courtyard of the Business Center. When he reached the steps at the first-floor entrance, Sun Lixing slipped and fell from a height of four steps, landing on the ground, resulting in an inability to move his limbs. The hospital diagnosed him with hyperextension injury of the cervical spinal cord combined with cervical nerve root traction injury, a laceration of the upper lip, an abrasion of the left arm, and a skin abrasion on the left leg. Sun Lixing applied to the Park Labor Bureau for a determination of work-related injury. On March 5, 2004, the Park Labor Bureau issued the "Decision on Determination of Work-related Injury" [(2004) No. 0001], which concluded that based on the injured employee's own application for work-related injury determination and the medical diagnosis certificate, combined with relevant investigation materials, and applying the standard for determining work-related injuries under Item 5 of Article 14 of the Regulations on Work-related Injury Insurance, there was no evidence to show that Sun Lixing's fall was caused by work-related reasons. Therefore, it decided not to recognize Sun Lixing's fall accident as a work-related injury. Sun Lixing, dissatisfied with the "Decision on Determination of Work-related Injury" of the Park Labor Bureau, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court.

Judgment

The Tianjin First Intermediate People's Court rendered Administrative Judgment (2005) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 39 on March 23, 2005: 1. Revoke the "Decision on Determination of Work-related Injury" [(2004) No. 0001] made by the Park Labor Bureau; 2. Order the Park Labor Bureau to re-make a specific administrative act within 60 days after the judgment takes effect. The Park Labor Bureau appealed. The Tianjin High People's Court rendered Administrative Judgment (2005) Jin Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 0034 on July 11, 2005: Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

Reasoning

The final effective judgment of the court held: The parties had no dispute that the Park Labor Bureau had the legal subject qualification and statutory authority for administrative law enforcement in this case, that the procedure for making the appealed decision on work-related injury determination was lawful, and that Sun Lixing fell during working hours. The points of contention in this case included: First, whether the place where Sun Lixing fell was within his "workplace"? Second, whether Sun Lixing fell "due to work-related reasons"? Third, whether Sun Lixing's negligence in carrying out his work duties affected the determination of work-related injury?

1. Regarding the issue of whether the place where Sun Lixing fell was within his "workplace"

Article 14, Item 1 of the Regulations on Work-related Injury Insurance stipulates that an injury suffered by an employee during working hours and at the workplace due to work-related reasons shall be recognized as a work-related injury. The term "workplace" in this provision refers to the place related to the employee's work duties. In situations with multiple workplaces, it also includes the reasonable area through which the employee travels between the different workplaces. In this case, the office of Zhongli Company on the eighth floor of the Business Center was Sun Lixing's workplace, and the parking spot for the car he needed to drive to complete the task of picking someone up at the airport was another workplace of Sun Lixing. The car was parked outside the first-floor entrance of the Business Center. To accomplish the driving task, Sun Lixing had to descend from the eighth floor of the Business Center to the parking spot outside the first-floor entrance. Therefore, the route from the eighth floor of the Business Center to the parking spot was a reasonable area for Sun Lixing to travel between his two workplaces and should also be recognized as part of Sun Lixing's workplace. The Park Labor Bureau's opinion that the place where Sun Lixing fell was not his workplace excludes the reasonable route for completing the work task from the workplace, which is not only inconsistent with the legislative intent but also contrary to common sense.

2. Regarding the issue of whether Sun Lixing fell "due to work-related reasons"

"Due to work-related reasons" as stipulated in Article 14, Item 1 of the Regulations on Work-related Injury Insurance refers to a correlation between the employee's injury and the work they are engaged in, i.e., a certain connection exists between the employee's injury and the work they were performing. To complete the assigned task of driving to pick someone up, Sun Lixing had to descend from the eighth floor of the Business Center to the first floor to enter the driver's seat of the car. This act was closely related to his work task and was objectively necessary for Sun Lixing to fulfill his work assignment; it was not a personal act unrelated to his work responsibilities. Therefore, Sun Lixing's fall on the steps at the first-floor entrance was caused by the need to complete the work task. The Park Labor Bureau's assertion that Sun Lixing's fall while descending the stairs had no direct causal relationship with his driving task and therefore did not constitute an injury "due to work-related reasons" lacks factual basis. Furthermore, after receiving the assignment from his superior to drive and pick someone up, Sun Lixing descended from the eighth floor of the Business Center to the first floor and fell on his way to the car parked in the courtyard. At that time, Sun Lixing had not yet left the company's premises, so this situation did not fall under "being on a business trip," but rather occurred during working hours and within the workplace.

3. Regarding the issue of whether Sun Lixing's negligence in carrying out his work duties affected the determination of work-related injury

Article 16 of the Regulations on Work-related Injury Insurance lists three statutory situations that exclude the determination of work-related injury: injuries caused by intentional crimes, drunkenness or drug use, or self-harm or suicide cannot be recognized as work-related injuries or treated as such. Negligence on the part of an employee during the performance of work duties is not among these statutory exclusions and cannot sever the connection between the employee's injury and the work they were performing. In work-related injury accidents, injured employees sometimes act negligently, carelessly, or inattentively. Work-related injury insurance is precisely an important system for sharing accident risks and providing labor protection. If the employee's subjective negligence were treated as a condition for excluding work-related injury recognition, it would violate the basic principle of "no-fault compensation" in work-related injury insurance and contradict the legislative purpose of the Regulations on Work-related Injury Insurance in protecting the legitimate rights and interests of workers. Accordingly, even if Sun Lixing was indeed careless while walking during his work, this would not affect the conclusion that his fall was "due to work-related reasons." The Park Labor Bureau's claim that the cause of Sun Lixing's fall was not the slippery steps due to rain or snow, but rather his own inattention, and therefore he did not fall "due to work-related reasons" and should not be recognized as having a work-related injury, lacks legal basis.

In conclusion, the decision of the Park Labor Bureau not to recognize Sun Lixing's injury as a work-related injury lacks factual basis and misapplies the law, and should be revoked according to law.

Guiding Case No. 41

Xuanyicheng et al. v. Quzhou City Bureau of Land and Resources, Zhejiang Province — Dispute over Withdrawal of Right to Use State-owned Land

(Adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on December 25, 2014)

Keywords Administrative litigation; Burden of proof; Failure to cite specific legal provisions; Application of erroneous law

Ruling Gist

Where an administrative agency fails to cite specific legal provisions when making a specific administrative act, and cannot prove during litigation that the specific administrative act conforms to specific legal provisions, it shall be deemed that the specific administrative act lacks legal basis and involves an erroneous application of law.

Ruling Summary

Article 32 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Basic Facts

The 18 plaintiffs, including Xuanyicheng, were residents of the teacher's dormitory building of Quzhou Fushan Middle School at No. 1 (formerly No. 14) Weining Lane, Kecheng District, Quzhou City, Zhejiang Province. On December 9, 2002, the Quzhou City Development and Planning Commission, upon reviewing a report from the third party, China Construction Bank Quzhou Branch (hereinafter referred to as the Quzhou Branch), approved the Quzhou Branch's project to expand its business premises by building an annex on the southeast side of its existing comprehensive business building. On the same day, the Quzhou City Planning Bureau prepared a site selection opinion for the construction project, noting that the Quzhou Branch intended to acquire and demolish the teacher's dormitory building of Fushan Middle School, covering an area of 205 square meters, to convert it into an open-air parking lot, to be implemented according to the detailed plan. On the 18th, the Quzhou City Planning Bureau prepared a red-line plan for the construction land of the Quzhou Branch's expanded business premises. On the 20th, the Quzhou City Planning Bureau issued a construction land planning permit, with the Quzhou Branch's construction project covering an area of 756 square meters. On the 25th, the defendant, Quzhou City Bureau of Land and Resources (hereinafter referred to as the Quzhou Bureau of Land), requested approval to withdraw the 187.6 square meters of state-owned land use rights of the residents of the Quzhou Fushan Middle School teacher's dormitory, which was approved by the Quzhou City People's Government. On the 31st of the same month, the Quzhou Bureau of Land issued the "Notice on Withdrawal of Right to Use State-owned Land" [Qu Shi Guo Tu (2002) No. 37] (hereinafter referred to as the "Notice"), informing the 18 plaintiffs, including Xuanyicheng, that their existing rights to use state-owned land would be withdrawn, along with their litigation rights. The Notice stated the name of the law on which the administrative decision was based but did not specify the particular legal provisions relied upon. The plaintiffs, dissatisfied, filed an administrative lawsuit.

Judgment

The Kecheng District People's Court of Quzhou City, Zhejiang Province, rendered Administrative Judgment (2003) Ke Xing Chu Zi No. 8 on August 29, 2003: Revoke the "Notice on Withdrawal of Right to Use State-owned Land" [Qu Shi Guo Tu (2002) No. 37] issued by the defendant, Quzhou City Bureau of Land and Resources on December 31, 2002. After the judgment was announced, neither party appealed, and the judgment became legally effective.

Reasoning

The final effective judgment of the court held: When the defendant, the Quzhou Bureau of Land, issued the "Notice," although it stated the name of the law on which the notice was based, it did not cite specific legal provisions. During the trial, the defendant argued that it made the contested specific administrative act pursuant to Article 58, Paragraph 1 of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Land Administration Law). Article 58, Paragraph 1 of the Land Administration Law stipulates: "Under any of the following circumstances, the land administration department of the relevant people's government may, upon approval by the original people's government that approved the land use or the people's government with the approval authority, withdraw the right to use state-owned land: (1) The land is needed for public interest; (2) The land use needs to be adjusted for the implementation of urban planning in old city reconstruction; ..." As the land administration department, the Quzhou Bureau of Land has the authority to manage and adjust the rights to use state-owned land within its jurisdiction under the Land Administration Law, but it must have a clear legal basis when exercising its powers. When the defendant issued the "Notice," it only stated that it was made pursuant to the Land Administration Law and relevant regulations of Zhejiang Province, but it did not cite specific legal provisions. Therefore, its specific administrative act lacked a clear legal basis and constituted an erroneous application of law.

In this case, the evidence provided by the Quzhou Bureau of Land, including the "Approval of the Construction Project Plan for Expanding Business Premises" [(2002) No. 35] from the Quzhou City Development and Planning Commission, the "Examination and Approval Form for Construction Project Site Selection Opinion," and the "Red-Line Plan for Construction Land for the Expansion of Business Premises of China Construction Bank Quzhou Branch," could hardly prove that the "Notice" it issued met the conditions under Article 58, Paragraph 1 of the Land Administration Law, specifically "the land is needed for public interest" or "the land use needs to be adjusted for the implementation of urban planning in old city reconstruction." The main evidence was insufficient, and thus the defendant's claim that its "Notice" was in compliance with the Land Administration Law was untenable. According to the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and related judicial interpretations, in administrative litigation, the defendant bears the burden of proof for the specific administrative act it has performed. If the defendant fails to provide the evidence and legal basis for the specific administrative act, the specific administrative act shall be deemed to have no evidence or legal basis.

In conclusion, the specific administrative act of the defendant withdrawing the right to use state-owned land was based on insufficient primary evidence and an erroneous application of law, and should be revoked.

Guiding Case No. 42

Zhu Hongwei v. Guangdong Provincial People's Procuratorate — Compensation for Unlawful Arrest

(Adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on December 25, 2014)

Keywords State compensation; Criminal compensation; Unlawful arrest; Compensation for mental distress

Ruling Gist

1. Where a state organ or its functionaries infringe upon a citizen's right to personal freedom while exercising their powers, seriously affecting the victim's normal work and life and causing them extreme mental anguish, this constitutes serious consequences of mental harm.

2. The amount of mental distress damages paid by the compensating organ shall be determined comprehensively based on specific circumstances such as the means, setting, and manner of the infringing act; the impact and consequences of the infringing act; and the local average standard of living.

Ruling Summary

Article 35 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China.

Basic Facts

The compensation claimant, Zhu Hongwei, applied, arguing that his erroneous detention by the procuratorial authorities caused him enormous material losses and mental harm. He requested that the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court uphold the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate's decision to pay compensation for the infringement of his personal freedom, and also order the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate to publish an apology in the newspaper, eliminate the impact, restore his reputation, pay 2,000,000 yuan in compensation for mental distress, and compensate for losses such as the impounded vehicle and auctioned property.

The Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate responded in its defense: Zhu Hongwei was detained without guilt for 873 days. The Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate lawfully decided to pay 124,254.09 yuan in compensation for the infringement of his personal freedom, offered a face-to-face apology to Zhu Hongwei, and visited relevant industrial and commercial administration departments and issued explanations to relevant banks to assist Zhu Hongwei in resuming his business operations. The Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate did not participate in the impoundment of the vehicle involved in the case and should not bear compensation liability for it. Zhu Hongwei failed to provide evidence of serious consequences of mental harm, his request for compensation for mental distress should not be supported, and his other requests fell outside the scope of state compensation.

Facts Found by the Court: On suspicion of contract fraud, Zhu Hongwei was criminally detained on July 25, 2005, and released on bail pending trial on August 26, 2005. On May 26, 2006, the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate approved the arrest of Zhu Hongwei by its Review Decision No. [2006] 4. On June 1, 2006, Zhu Hongwei was arrested. On September 11, 2008, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, Guangdong Province, rendered a judgment acquitting Zhu Hongwei due to insufficient evidence for the charges. On September 19, 2008, Zhu Hongwei was released. Zhu Hongwei was detained for a total of 875 days. On March 15, 2011, Zhu Hongwei applied to the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate for state compensation on the grounds of unlawful arrest. On July 19, 2011, the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate issued Criminal Compensation Decision [2011] No. 1: Compensation for infringement of personal freedom of 124,254.09 yuan (142.33 yuan x 873 days) was paid based on the national average daily wage standard for the year 2010; offered a verbal apology and lawfully provided facilities within its functional scope to assist Zhu Hongwei in resuming production; the request for compensation for mental distress was not supported.

It was further found that: (1) Zhu Hongwei's daughter, Zhu Moumou, was under 18 years old at the time of Zhu Hongwei's criminal detention and her depression had not healed as of 2012. (2) Shenzhen Yihe Industrial Co., Ltd. had been operated by Zhu Hongwei as its Chairman and legal representative since 2004, but had not participated in annual inspections since 2005. (3) In a separate case, Zhu Hongwei applied for compensation from the Shenzhen Municipal Public Security Bureau for the loss of the impounded vehicle. The Compensation Committee of the Guangdong High People's Court dismissed Zhu Hongwei's compensation application on the grounds that he had no evidence to prove he was the vehicle's owner or that he had suffered actual loss. (4) On September 5, 2011, the Guangdong High People's Court, Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate, and Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department jointly issued the "Summary of Minutes of the Symposium on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Compensation for Mental Distress in State Compensation Cases" [Yue Gao Fa (2011) No. 382]. After this summary was issued, the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate indicated that it could pay compensation for mental distress pursuant to it.

Judgment

The Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court rendered State Compensation Decision (2011) Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 4 on June 18, 2012: Affirmed Item 2 of the Criminal Compensation Decision [2011] No. 1 of the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate; Revoked Items 1 and 3 of the Criminal Compensation Decision [2011] No. 1 of the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate; Ordered the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate to pay Zhu Hongwei 142,318.75 yuan in compensation for the infringement of his personal freedom; Ordered the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate to pay Zhu Hongwei 50,000 yuan in compensation for mental distress; Dismissed Zhu Hongwei's other claims for compensation.

Reasoning

The Supreme People's Court held that the compensation claimant, Zhu Hongwei, submitted his request for compensation to the compensating organ, the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate, on March 15, 2011. This case should be governed by the revised State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China. The actual period of Zhu Hongwei's detention was 875 days. The Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate's calculation of 873 days was erroneous and should be corrected. According to Article 6 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the People's Courts' Implementation of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China," where the Compensation Committee revokes a compensation decision of the compensating organ that has not yet taken effect, the compensation standard shall be the national average daily wage for the year prior to the year this compensation decision is made, which is 162.65 yuan for 2011. Therefore, the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate should pay Zhu Hongwei 142,318.75 yuan in compensation for the infringement of his personal freedom for 875 days, calculated based on the 2011 national average daily wage standard. After Zhu Hongwei was acquitted, the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate had already decided to offer a verbal apology to Zhu Hongwei and provide facilities to assist him in resuming production, thereby eliminating the impact and restoring his reputation within the scope of the infringing act. This decision should be affirmed. Zhu Hongwei's additional request for the Guandong Provincial People's Procuratorate to publish an apology in a newspaper is not supported.

Zhu Hongwei was detained for 875 days, which also affected his normal family life and company operations, causing him extreme mental anguish. It should be determined that the consequences of mental harm were serious. Regarding the compensation for mental distress claimed by Zhu Hongwei, based on the fact that Shenzhen Yihe Industrial Co., Ltd. could not operate normally since Zhu Hongwei's detention in 2005, that his daughter suffered from unhealed depression, the reference standards for compensation for mental distress in Guangdong Province as clarified in "Summary of Minutes of the Symposium on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Compensation for Mental Distress in State Compensation Cases" [Yue Gao Fa (2011) No. 382], combined with the consultation and coordination situation and the local average standard of living, the amount is determined to be 50,000 yuan. Zhu Hongwei's other requests are not supported.

Guiding Case No. 43

Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd. Haikou Binhai Avenue (Tianfu Hotel) Securities Business Department v. — Compensation for Erroneous Enforcement

(Adopted upon deliberation by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 25, 2014)

Keywords: State compensation  Judicial compensation  Erroneous execution  Execution reversal

Ruling Gist

1. Where a compensation claimant applies for state compensation on the grounds that the people's court has engaged in illegal infringement as provided in Article 38 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, the people's court shall examine both whether the judicial act complained of by the compensation claimant is illegal and whether the state compensation liability should be incurred.

2. Where a people's court, in hearing an execution objection case, renders a ruling to revoke the original execution act because the execution settlement agreement between the parties on which the original execution act was based infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a third party not involved in the case, and restores the executed property to the state before execution, such revocation ruling and execution reversal act do not constitute an erroneous execution as provided in Article 38 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China.

Relevant Legal Provision

Article 38 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The compensation claimant, Guotai Junan Securities Co., Ltd., Haikou Binhai Avenue (Tianfu Hotel) Securities Business Department (hereinafter referred to as Guotai Haikou Business Department), applied for compensation on the grounds that the Hainan High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Hainan High Court), without conducting a retrial of the original effective judgment and its rulings (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi Nos. 9-10, 9-11, 9-12, and 9-13 (hereinafter referred to as No. 9-10, 9-11, 9-12, and 9-13 rulings respectively), issued Ruling (1999) Qiong Gao Fa Zhi Zi No. 9-16 (hereinafter referred to as No. 9-16 ruling) and executed reversal based thereon, revoking the original No. 9-11, 9-12, and 9-13 rulings, thereby causing Guotai Haikou Business Department to lose the lawfully acquired real property. It requested a finding of illegality and state compensation.

The Hainan High Court responded: Its No. 9-16 ruling merely corrected errors in the previous execution rulings and did not change the original execution basis, thus no trial supervision procedure was required. The No. 9-16 ruling and its execution reversal act were based on the established execution objection of a third party not involved in the case, restoring the disputed real property to the ownership status as at the commencement of the execution case. This act had no causal relationship with the debt confirmed by the judgment in favor of Guotai Haikou Business Department or its unspecified loss claim. Guotai Haikou Business Department's compensation claim was untenable and should be dismissed.

The court found through trial: On September 21, 1998, the Hainan High Court rendered Civil Judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8 in the case of Guotai Haikou Business Department v. Hainan International Leasing Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hainan Leasing Company) concerning a securities repurchase dispute, ordering Hainan Leasing Company to pay Guotai Haikou Business Department the principal of securities repurchase funds of RMB 36,200,000 and interest thereon up to November 30, 1997 of RMB 16,362,296; Hainan Leasing Company was to pay Guotai Haikou Business Department interest on the principal of RMB 36,200,000 calculated at an annual rate of 18% from December 1, 1997 until full payment.

In December 1998, Guotai Haikou Business Department applied to the Hainan High Court for enforcement of that judgment. After accepting the case, the Hainan High Court issued an enforcement notice to Hainan Leasing Company and found that the company had no assets available for execution. Hainan Leasing Company claimed it had a matured claim against a third party, Hainan Zhongbiao Property Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongbiao Company). Zhongbiao Company acknowledged this and expressed willingness to directly offset part of its debt to Hainan Leasing Company by using part of the Jingrui Mansion real property to compensate Guotai Haikou Business Department. The Hainan High Court accordingly made Ruling No. 9-10 on June 13, 2000, sealing up part of the Jingrui Mansion real property and announcing it on the same day. On June 29 of the same year, Guotai Haikou Business Department, Hainan Leasing Company, and Zhongbiao Company jointly signed an Execution Settlement Agreement, stipulating that Hainan Leasing Company and Zhongbiao Company would use part of the Jingrui Mansion real property owned by Zhongbiao Company to offset Guotai Haikou Business Department's debt. Accordingly, on June 30, the Hainan High Court made Ruling No. 9-11, approving the settlement agreement.

During the process of handling the transfer procedures, third parties not involved in the case, the Hainan Development Bank Liquidation Group (hereinafter referred to as Haifa Bank Liquidation Group) and Hainan Chuangren Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chuangren Company), filed execution objections on the grounds that the real property used to offset the debt in Ruling No. 9-11 of the Hainan High Court belonged to them and that the ruling infringed upon their lawful rights and interests. After review, the Hainan High Court made Ruling No. 9-12 and Ruling No. 9-13 respectively, dismissing the objections. On March 14, 2002, Guotai Haikou Business Department, pursuant to Ruling No. 9-11, completed the registration of ownership transfer of the aforesaid offset real property to its own name and paid the relevant taxes and fees. After Haifa Bank Liquidation Group and Chuangren Company appealed, the Hainan High Court conducted another review and found: Ruling No. 9-11 used the real property that former Jintong City Credit Cooperative (later merged into Hainan Development Bank) had purchased from Zhongbiao Company and paid most of the purchase price for as property of Zhongbiao Company to offset the debt to Guotai Haikou Business Department, thereby harming the interests of Haifa Bank Liquidation Group. This was indeed improper. Haifa Bank Liquidation Group's objection was justified, and Chuangren Company's objection should be resolved through litigation proceedings. Accordingly, on July 31, 2003, the Hainan High Court made Ruling No. 9-16, revoking Rulings No. 9-11, 9-12, and 9-13, and ordering the transfer back of the real property previously offset to its state before execution.

On December 18, 2004, the Haikou Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Haikou Intermediate Court), in the real property confirmation dispute case with Haifa Bank Liquidation Group as plaintiff, Zhongbiao Company as defendant, and Chuangren Company as third party, rendered Civil Judgment (2003) Hai Zhong Fa Min Zai Zi No. 37, confirming that the original offset real property belonged to Chuangren Company and Haifa Bank Liquidation Group respectively. This judgment has become legally effective. In June 2005, Guotai Haikou Business Department applied to the Haikou Local Taxation Bureau for a tax refund, and the bureau refunded the deed tax to Guotai Haikou Business Department. On August 4, 2006, the Hainan High Court made Civil Ruling No. 9-18, ruling to terminate the enforcement of Civil Judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8 on the grounds that Hainan Leasing Company had been ruled bankrupt for debt repayment and the grounds for the request by Hainan Leasing Company's liquidation group to terminate enforcement were established.

The debt under Civil Judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8 was transferred by agreement to Guotai Junan Investment Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guotai Investment Company) by July 2004. On November 29, 2005, Hainan Leasing Company applied to the Haikou Intermediate Court for bankruptcy liquidation. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Guotai Investment Company reported to the administrator of Hainan Leasing Company the relevant claims, including those confirmed by Civil Judgment (1998) Qiong Jing Chu Zi No. 8. On March 31, 2009, the Haikou Intermediate Court made Civil Ruling (2005) Hai Zhong Fa Po Zi No. 4-350, terminating the bankruptcy liquidation proceedings, and Guotai Investment Company's claims were not satisfied.

On December 27, 2010, Guotai Haikou Business Department applied to the Hainan High Court for state compensation on the grounds that Ruling No. 9-16 and the act of the Hainan High Court were illegal and that the real property offset under Ruling No. 9-11 should be returned or relevant losses compensated. On July 4, 2011, the Hainan High Court made Compensation Decision (2011) Qiong Fa Pei Zi No. 1, deciding not to compensate Guotai Haikou Business Department's compensation application. Dissatisfied with that decision, Guotai Haikou Business Department applied to the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court for a compensation decision.

Judgment

The Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court made State Compensation Decision (2011) Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 3 on March 23, 2012: Upholding the Compensation Decision (2011) Qiong Fa Pei Zi No. 1 of the Hainan High People's Court.

Reasoning

The Supreme People's Court held: The executed person, Hainan Leasing Company, had no ability to satisfy its debts. Because it had a matured claim against the third party, Zhongbiao Company, and Zhongbiao Company did not object and acknowledged the debt, Zhongbiao Company concealed the fact that it had already signed a sale contract with a third party not involved in the case and received most of the purchase price, and together with Guotai Haikou Business Department and Hainan Leasing Company, the three parties reached an Execution Settlement Agreement. The Hainan High Court accordingly made Ruling No. 9-11. However, the above execution settlement agreement infringed upon the lawful rights and interests of the third party not involved in the case, and the disputed real property rights obtained by Guotai Haikou Business Department based thereon should not be protected by law. Ruling No. 9-16 of the Hainan High Court, in the execution proceedings, upon review and establishment of the execution objection raised by the third party not involved in the case, revoked the original Ruling No. 9-11 and restored the executed disputed real property to its state before execution. This ruling and the execution reversal act did not violate legal provisions and were confirmed by the findings of the effective Civil Judgment (2003) Hai Zhong Fa Min Zai Zi No. 37 of the Haikou Intermediate Court; the substantive handling was not improper. The substantive reason for the failure to realize Guotai Haikou Business Department's debt was that Hainan Leasing Company lacked the ability to satisfy its debts. Even though Guotai Haikou Business Department and its debt assignee filed claims in the bankruptcy proceedings, they still could not obtain satisfaction. There was no legal causal connection between the failure to realize the debt and Ruling No. 9-16 of the Hainan High Court and its execution act. Therefore, Ruling No. 9-16 of the Hainan High Court and its execution reversal act did not fall within the circumstances of erroneous execution as provided in the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China and relevant judicial interpretations.

Guiding Case No. 44

Bu Xinguang's Application for Criminal Compensation for Illegal Recovery

(Adopted upon deliberation by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 25, 2014)

Keywords: State compensation  Criminal compensation  Criminal recovery  Return of stolen goods

Ruling Gist

Where a public security organ, pursuant to a legally effective criminal judgment of a people's court, returns the stolen goods ordered to be recovered to the aggrieved unit, and does not infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the compensation claimant, this does not fall within the circumstances provided in Item 1 of Article 18 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, and the state compensation liability shall not be incurred.

Relevant Legal Provision

Article 18 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The compensation claimant, Bu Xinguang, filed a compensation application with the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court on the grounds that the Criminal Compensation Decision Wan Gong Xing Pei Zi (2011) No. 1 of the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department and the Criminal Compensation Review Decision Gong Gong Xing Pei Fu Zi (2011) No. 1 of the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Ministry of Public Security) did not conform to the facts and improperly applied the law, alleging that the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department exceeded its authority in handling economic disputes, illegally used the "Shenkeng Village Land" purchased by him to offset bank debts, and requested compensation for economic losses of RMB 3,166,000, among other claims.

The court found through trial: The compensation claimant, Bu Xinguang, was placed under criminal investigation by the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department on suspicion of the crime of forging company seals, the crime of illegally issuing financial instruments, and the crime of misappropriating funds. He was arrested on September 5, 1999. Before his arrest, he was the general manager of Shenzhen Xinhui Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinhui Company). On November 20, 2001, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court rendered Criminal Judgment (2001) He Xing Chu Zi No. 68, finding that during the period from January 1995 when Bu Xinguang began contracting to operate the Shenzhen Securities Business Department of Anhui Trust and Investment Company (hereinafter referred to as Anxin Securities Department), without the authorization of Anhui Trust and Investment Company (hereinafter referred to as Anxin Company), he arranged for his employed personnel to privately engrave and use company seals exclusively belonging to Anxin Company, and used these false seals to forge a power of attorney from Anxin Company's legal representative, a certificate of legal representative, and a guarantee document submitted to the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, thereby obtaining the business qualifications of Anxin Securities Department. His conduct constituted the crime of forging seals. During the period of contracting to operate Anxin Securities Department, Bu Xinguang, in violation of financial management regulations, twice issued false financial proof to others, causing significant economic losses of RMB 10,320,000, which constituted the crime of illegally issuing financial instruments. During the contracting and operation process, as the general manager of Anxin Securities Department, taking advantage of his position, he directly or indirectly misappropriated RMB 91,732,286 of the funds of Anxin Securities Department for investment and various expenses of Xinhui Company, which he personally owned, unrelated to the business operations of Anxin Securities Department, and the economic losses caused were borne by Anxin Securities Department and Anxin Company as legal liability. This should be regarded as Bu Xinguang misappropriating the securities department's funds for personal use, constituting the crime of misappropriating funds. After the crime was discovered, the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department recovered stolen money of RMB 16,890,500, stolen goods and housing equivalent to RMB 16,270,000; sealed up real property with an investment value of RMB 28,400,000 and land use rights with an investment value of RMB 19,500,000 owned by Xinhui Company, totaling RMB 81,060,500. Bu Xinguang committed multiple crimes and should be punished for several offenses. The judgment was: 1. Bu Xinguang was sentenced to two years' imprisonment for the crime of forging company seals; eight years' imprisonment for the crime of illegally issuing financial instruments; ten years' imprisonment for the crime of misappropriating funds; the combined sentence was fifteen years' imprisonment. 2. The stolen money and stolen goods totaling RMB 81,060,500 were to be recovered. Bu Xinguang appealed. The Anhui High People's Court, on February 22, 2002, rendered Criminal Ruling (2002) Wan Xing Zhong Zi No. 34, dismissing the appeal and upholding the original judgment. The land use rights sealed up and ordered to be recovered as determined by the above criminal judgment referred to the "Shenkeng Village Land" use rights invested by Bu Xinguang in the name of Xinhui Company. On August 4, 2009, Bu Xinguang was released upon completion of his sentence.

It was also found: After the criminal case of Bu Xinguang was discovered, Shenzhen Development Bank Renminqiao Sub-branch (formerly Shenzhen Development Bank Business Department, hereinafter referred to as Shenfa Bank), on the grounds of a debt dispute with Bu Xinguang, Anxin Securities Department, and Anxin Company concerning a 2500万元拆借 borrowing, filed a civil lawsuit with the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court on December 28, 1999, case number (2000) Shen Zhong Fa Jing Diao Chu Zi No. 72. Shenfa Bank also filed civil lawsuits simultaneously with the Shenzhen Luohu District People's Court on March 10, 2000, on the grounds of disputes over guaranteed loans, borrowing fund contracts, and margin deposit agreements with Anxin Securities Department and Anxin Company, which were accepted under case numbers (2000) Shen Luo Fa Jing Yi Chu Zi No. 372 and (2000) Shen Luo Fa Jing Yi Chu Zi No. 373. On April 19, 2000, the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department sent a letter to the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court and the Luohu District People's Court, requesting that the courts, pursuant to Article 12 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Involvement of Criminal Suspicions in the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases, suspend the civil cases and transfer them to the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department for unified investigation. On July 15, 2000, the Luohu District People's Court transferred the civil cases it had accepted, (2000) Shen Luo Fa Jing Yi Chu Zi No. 372 and (2000) Shen Luo Fa Jing Yi Chu Zi No. 373, to the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department. On August 24, 2000, the Criminal Investigation Team of the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department sealed up the "Shenkeng Village Land". Regarding the case of Shenfa Bank v. Anxin Securities Department and Anxin Company for a borrowing debt dispute of RMB 25,000,000 under (2000) Shen Zhong Fa Jing Diao Chu Zi No. 72, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, after trial, held that the case involved criminal offenses and, on September 21, 2001, transferred the case to the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department for investigation and handling, simultaneously notifying Shenfa Bank, Anxin Company, and Anxin Securities Department that the civil case had been transferred to the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department. After Criminal Judgment (2001) He Xing Chu Zi No. 68 of the Hefei Intermediate People's Court became effective, the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department unsealed the "Shenkeng Village Land" and returned the recovered land use rights to the aggrieved unit, Anxin Securities Department, to offset the debt of RMB 25,000,000 that Bu Xinguang, in the name of Anxin Securities Department, had borrowed from Shenfa Bank in the civil case (2000) Shen Zhong Fa Jing Diao Chu Zi No. 72 investigated by the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department.

It was further found: After the criminal case of Bu Xinguang was discovered, Shenfa Bank, on the grounds that Anxin Securities Department had borrowed RMB 20,000,000 from it, of which only RMB 12,000,000 had been repaid, and the remaining RMB 8,000,000 was overdue, filed a lawsuit with the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court against Bu Xinguang, Anxin Securities Department, and Anxin Company based on a bond repurchase agreement dispute, seeking joint and several repayment of the outstanding RMB 8,000,000 and interest of RMB 3,000,000. On November 9, 1999, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (1998) Shen Zhong Fa Jing Yi Chu Zi No. 311: Bu Xinguang was to repay RMB 2,570,016 to Shenfa Bank, plus interest for the period of using RMB 20,000,000; if Bu Xinguang's property was insufficient to satisfy the debt, Anxin Securities Department and Anxin Company were to bear supplementary liability. That civil judgment was settled during enforcement by a settlement agreement between Shenfa Bank and Anxin Company, with other property used to offset the debt.

Judgment

The Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court, on November 24, 2011, made a decision of the Compensation Committee (2011) Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 1: Upholding the Criminal Compensation Decision Wan Gong Xing Pei Zi (2011) No. 1 of the Anhui Provincial Public Security Department and the Criminal Compensation Review Decision Gong Pei Fu Zi (2011) No. 1 of the Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China.

Reasoning

The Supreme People's Court held: During the period of contracting to operate Anxin Securities Department, Bu Xinguang, without authorization from Anxin Company, privately engraved and used the seal of Anxin Company, violated financial management regulations by issuing false financial proof to others, and took advantage of his position to misappropriate RMB 91,732,286 of Anxin Securities Department's funds. This was confirmed by Criminal Judgment (2001) He Xing Chu Zi No. 68 of the Hefei Intermediate People's Court, which found him guilty of forging seals, illegally issuing financial instruments, and misappropriating funds. The judgment ordered the recovery of stolen money and stolen goods totaling RMB 81,060,500 (including land use rights valued at RMB 19,500,000), including the "Shenkeng Village Land" use rights invested by Bu Xinguang in the name of Xinhui Company. Bu Xinguang's claim that the part of the land use rights purchased with funds from Xinhui Company was his personal lawful property was unfounded. The legally effective criminal judgment of the people's court had already ordered the recovery of the "Shenkeng Village Land" use rights valued at RMB 19,500,000 invested by Xinhui Company as part of the stolen money and stolen goods from Bu Xinguang's crime of misappropriating funds. Bu Xinguang had no right to claim state compensation for property that had been ordered to be recovered by a legally effective judgment of the people's court.

Regarding Bu Xinguang's claim that the Anhui Provincial Public Security Bureau used the "Shenkeng Village land" to offset his debt of RMB 800,000 owed to Shenzhen Development Bank, causing direct property losses of RMB 3,166,000. After the incident suspected of Bu Xinguang's crime was uncovered, Shenzhen Development Bank filed a lawsuit against Bu Xinguang, Anxin Securities Department, and Anxin Company concerning the RMB 8,000,000 bond repurchase agreement. The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court rendered Civil Judgment No. (1998) Shen Zhong Fa Jing Yi Chu Zi No. 311, which was already enforced. This case is not the same civil case as the debt dispute involving a loan of RMB 25,000,000 that Shenzhen Development Bank filed against Bu Xinguang, Anxin Securities Department, and Anxin Company, which the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court transferred to the Anhui Provincial Public Security Bureau for investigation on September 21, 2001, under (2000) Shen Zhong Fa Jing Tiao Chu Zi No. 72. After the criminal judgment became effective, the Anhui Provincial Public Security Bureau returned the right to use the "Shenkeng Village land" valued at RMB 19,500,000, which had been ordered to be confiscated by the judgment, to the victim of the case it investigated involving Bu Xinguang borrowing RMB 25,000,000 from Shenzhen Development Bank in the name of Anxin Securities Department. This action had a factual basis and did not harm Bu Xinguang's interests. Bu Xinguang's claim that the Anhui Provincial Public Security Bureau used the "Shenkeng Village land" to offset his debt of RMB 800,000 to Shenzhen Development Bank is inconsistent with the facts. Bu Xinguang's request for the Anhui Provincial Public Security Bureau to compensate for the losses of RMB 3,166,000 caused by the allegedly illegal return of the "Shenkeng Village land" lacks factual and legal basis.

In summary, the "Shenkeng Village land" was confiscated by Criminal Ruling No. (2002) Wan Xing Zhong Zi No. 34 of the Anhui High People's Court. The claim by the compensation claimant, Bu Xinguang, that the Anhui Provincial Public Security Bureau illegally returned the land, causing him losses of RMB 3,166,000, has no legal basis. His other claims lack factual basis and do not comply with the provisions of the State Compensation Law, and are therefore not supported.
